# the contributor audit: sharp retained-volume comparison and latent quantile response

## 1. Sharp E–T–V theorem: analytic PASS

Source:
`candidate da4697fe92a737cb`.
the contributor and Defect independently obtained the same two-sided section proof;
Slab then independently derived it and audited the complete source.

The actual optimizing hinge yields one retained convex cap D of volume T
and centroid y. In the noncentroid case its threshold normalizes to t=-1.
The homothety of D toward a highest point gives the survival lower bound
and hence B<=d. The comparison cone restriction has the same retained
mass and first moment. Concavity of section roots gives a single interval
of positive difference; matching both moments forces negative differences
at both ends. Subtracting the secant of a convex test gives the claimed
convex order. Concavity then controls the entire exterior section law,
where matching the remaining volume gives the one-crossing stochastic
comparison. Both are in the correct direction for the cone's increasing,
strictly convex, admissible projective kernel.

The evaluated integral gives exactly

    E <= (d+1)T-d T^(1+1/d)V^(-1/d).

Strict comparison equality forces the entire conical section profile.
Endpoint section convergence and equal-volume containment reconstruct the
actual cone. The retained subcone's centroid supplies axiality; the converse
uses full, not just axial, energy stationarity. The centroid case T=V and
the interval identity E=2T-T^2/V are separately correct. In particular

    V F_d^(-1)(E/V)<=Gamma_d T

for every interior mark. This is a pointwise domination, so no further
joint-concavity argument is required to close the scalar energy bridge.

The companion nested-simplex counterexample in
`candidate 3208a2842914cf02`
is exact in every d>=2. Its barycentrics, projective integral and strictly
concave G(q) prove the certified cap mass decreases under inclusion,
despite increasing E and nondecreasing true raw depth. The endpoint-offset
example correctly keeps volumes, energies and opposite numeric offsets
fixed while its cap sum tends to only Gamma_d V. It does not hold the
middle fiber geometry fixed or claim to defeat geometry-aware methods.
the contributor rerun:1,094 exact checks PASS.

## 2. Frustum near-quantile theorem: analytic PASS

Source:
`candidate 19899b61b9ca5f3a`.

The exact slice integral, small quantile root and proper-cut status agree.
Normal recovery uses coefficients g/(3 beta), so its multiplier order is
1/|beta|, while aggregate slack is O(|beta|). The general C2 lemma explicitly
retains its extra regularity premise. Its second normal derivative is
minus the threshold derivative of the squared-perturbation section moment,
with the correct sign. The resulting quadratic source bound is only an
upper bound unless the separately proved all-normal gap is available.

The top-facet convex erosion has a genuinely nonzero primary response,
so unrestricted blown-up stresses diverge. On the stipulated primary-
neutral face, the facewise coarea derivative produces a finite angular
response. Its regularity, transversality and trace assumptions are stated;
supporting coincidences and arbitrary measurable speeds are not silently
included. the contributor independently checked the exact horizontal section moment
for the first normal: it is -4 c_beta, as required by -2 c_beta v_1.

The common source-motion term 4gh and normal-motion term
-(2gA/9)sum B_(i,t) survive the blow-up. The actual translated homothety
has R'_0=-4a and actual deepest velocity h=a, giving exact cancellation.
Nearby quantile caps do not form an original positive circuit and exclude
the old source. Consequently this theorem neither supplies a neutral
deepest path nor upgrades a limiting normal certificate to a cap cover.

## 3. Boundary stress and interior rigidity: analytic PASS

Source:
`candidate ca19899f75c1a20d`.

Conditional Jensen equality gives exactly affine-contact confinement.
It does not give equality for an arbitrary strictly convex test. The
four-fiber example has explicit all-normal depth, unique deepest point,
and full martingale marginals. Its central surplus must leave the deepest
fiber even for another coupling. The R4 upgrade uses already audited
full criticality and the exact short martingale certificate, preserving
strict proper-minor count quotas. Its source/target central masses force
outgoing boundary mass sigma/30 in every coupling.

Boundary-zero T/E values cannot mark destinations as deepest. Even the
normal-weighted interior centroid marks have the same full T and E while
being strictly shallower. Neither example satisfies strict bad depth,
which remains an essential possible additional premise.

The compatible-translates endpoint has Two-sided's independent audit.
Projection Doignon legitimately works because the graph hull has one
point per integer fiber. A whole rigid translated family satisfies the
sharp bound; a proper rigid class pays only its own mass. There is no
justified combination of the classes' separate selected points.

No OC proof or complete mixed assembly is asserted by these audits.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
